````math
## Appendix G Hash Function and PRNG

In this part, we explain the hash functions used by the agents to turn
the context into a seed (i.e., an integer), and detail the PRNG
algorithm we use in our library.

#### Hash functions

As stated in
[Section A.3](#A1.SS3 "A.3 Context Seeding ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
we assume that the hashing function is without collision, i.e., two
contexts that are different should return a different hash. In
particular, prior works used weaker hash functions that had a high
probability of collisions. We assume we have a tuple
$`(x_{1},\dots,x_{k})\in\mathbb{N}^{k}`$ of integers (token IDs or
lexical classes $`\mathcal{G}(\omega_{t})`$). All arithmetic is on
unsigned 64-bit integers (i.e., modulo $`2^{64}`$) unless stated
otherwise, $`\oplus`$ is the bitwise XOR, and $`\gg`$ the right shift.

*SplitMix64 hash:* We chain the SplitMix64 finalizer
$`m(x)=y_{2}\oplus(y_{2}\gg 31)`$, with
$`y_{1}=(x\oplus(x\gg 30))\cdot\texttt{0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9}`$ and
$`y_{2}=(y_{1}\oplus(y_{1}\gg 27))\cdot\texttt{0x94d049bb133111eb}`$.
The context hash is

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
h_{0}=\texttt{0x243f6a8885a308d3},\qquad h_{j}=m\bigl(h_{j-1}\oplus m(x_{j}+j)\bigr),\qquad a_{t}=h_{k},
``` |  |

where the offset $`+j`$ makes the hash order-sensitive. The hash is not
injective, but with $`64`$-bit outputs a collision among $`n`$ contexts
has probability at most $`n^{2}/2^{65}`$.

*Rotation first hash:* packs the context injectively, so the
no-collision assumption holds exactly. However, it is only valid for
context sizes up to two. A context of length one is encoded as
$`a_{t}=x_{1}+1`$, and one of length two as
$`a_{t}=2^{41}+2^{20}x_{1}+x_{2}`$, which is injective for vocabularies
below $`2^{20}`$.

*Rolling polynomial hash:* a rolling polynomial hash with a counter.
This is the hash used with Ladder context
seeding ([Section A.3](#A1.SS3 "A.3 Context Seeding ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
Given the lexical classes $`g_{t}=\mathcal{G}(\omega_{t})`$, a context
of width $`w\leq 4`$ ending at $`t`$ is hashed as

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
K_{w}=\Bigl(\sum_{i=0}^{w-1}g_{t-i}\,\varphi^{\,w-1-i}\Bigr)\oplus(w\cdot\texttt{0x2545F4914F6CDD1D}),\qquad\varphi=\texttt{0x9E3779B97F4A7C15},
``` |  |

where the XOR with a width-dependent constant separates contexts of
different lengths. Let $`n`$ be the number of earlier occurrences of
$`K_{w}`$ in the text, and $`w^{\star}`$ the width selected by the
ladder. The seed is then

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
a_{t}=\bigl\lfloor\mathrm{fmix}_{64}\bigl(8192\,K_{w^{\star}}+n\bigr)/2^{32}\bigr\rfloor,
``` |  |

where $`\mathrm{fmix}_{64}`$ is the MurmurHash3 finalizer and $`8192`$
is the maximum tally, so that repeated contexts with different counts
get different seeds. Unlike the two previous hashes, the seed has only
$`32`$ bits and collides after roughly $`2^{16}`$ distinct contexts.

#### PRNG

Given a seed $`a_{t}`$, a candidate token $`v`$, and the 64-bit private
key $`\xi`$, the PRNG returns the score $`U_{a_{t},v}\in[0,1)`$. We
require it to be stateless, i.e., $`U_{a_{t},v}`$ depends only on
$`(\xi,a_{t},v)`$, so that the detector recovers exactly the scores used
at generation.

*Philox:* this is the PRNG we implemented as part of our library and
used for all baselines. It uses the counter-based Philox4x32-10 block
cipher ([Salmon et al., 2011](#bib.bib27)), which maps a 128-bit counter
and a 64-bit key to $`4`$ pseudorandom 32-bit words
$`(y_{0},y_{1},y_{2},y_{3})`$. With $`A`$ a bijective 32-bit avalanche
($`x\mapsto x\oplus(x\gg 16)`$, multiply by 0x7FEB352D,
$`x\oplus(x\gg 15)`$, multiply by 0x846CA68B, $`x\oplus(x\gg 16)`$), the
score is

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
(y_{0},\dots,y_{3})=\mathrm{Philox}_{\xi}\bigl(A(v),\,A(a_{t}),\,0,\,0\bigr),\qquad U_{a_{t},v}=\lfloor y_{0}/2^{9}\rfloor\,2^{-23},
``` |  |

where the avalanche disperses adjacent token IDs before Philox, and
$`23`$ bits fill the float32 mantissa. Independent Channels $`c`$ use
the candidate $`v+2^{18}c`$, which never collides with a real token ID.

*High-precision Philox:* similar to Philox, but the 64-bit seed and the
token are packed injectively into the counter:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle(y_{0},\dots,y_{3})`$ | $`\displaystyle=\mathrm{Philox}_{\xi}\bigl(v,\,a_{t}\bmod 2^{32},\,\lfloor a_{t}/2^{32}\rfloor,\,\texttt{0xC0C0A123}\bigr),`$ |  |
|  | $`\displaystyle U_{a_{t},v}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\bigl(2^{26}\lfloor y_{0}/2^{6}\rfloor+\lfloor y_{1}/2^{6}\rfloor\bigr)\,2^{-52}+2^{-53}.`$ |  |

Since the counter is injective in $`(a_{t},v)`$, distinct (seed, token)
pairs always map to distinct Philox counters, hence to pseudorandomly
independent scores. When several scores are needed per (seed, token)
pair (e.g., the three coordinates for RotationFirst), the seed is
replaced by $`2^{6}a_{t}+d`$, reserving the low $`6`$ bits for the index
$`d`$.

*SplitMix64 PRF:* reuses the SplitMix64 finalizer $`m`$ from the
*SplitMix64 hash*, with the domain-separation constants
$`c_{1}=\texttt{0xa4093822299f31d0}`$ and
$`c_{2}=\texttt{0x082efa98ec4e6c89}`$:

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
s=m\bigl(a_{t}\oplus m(\xi\oplus c_{1})\bigr),\qquad s^{\prime}=m\bigl(s\oplus m(v\oplus c_{2})\bigr),\qquad U_{a_{t},v}=\bigl(\lfloor s^{\prime}/2^{12}\rfloor+\tfrac{1}{2}\bigr)\,2^{-52},
``` |  |

where $`52`$ bits fill the float64 mantissa, and the midpoint
$`+\tfrac{1}{2}`$ keeps $`U_{a_{t},v}\in(0,1)`$ so that
$`\Phi^{-1}(U_{a_{t},v})`$ is always finite. Independent Channels $`c`$
use the key $`\xi\oplus(c\cdot\texttt{0x9e3779b97f4a7c15})`$.

## Appendix H ConcordMark and RotationFirst

We describe the schemes used
in [Section 4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Independent Evaluation of the Best Directions ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").
For low and high variants, the generation is shared and only the
detector differs.

### H.1 ConcordMark

#### Key components

We describe precisely the ConcordMark generation algorithm
in [Algorithm 4](#alg4 "In Key components ‣ H.1 ConcordMark ‣ Appendix H ConcordMark and RotationFirst ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
and both detector variants
in [Algorithms 5](#alg5 "In Key components ‣ H.1 ConcordMark ‣ Appendix H ConcordMark and RotationFirst ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
and [6](#alg6 "Algorithm 6 ‣ Key components ‣ H.1 ConcordMark ‣ Appendix H ConcordMark and RotationFirst ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").
ConcordMark uses Lexical group only for context seeding. Let
$`\mathcal{G}:\Sigma\rightarrow\mathbb{N}`$ be the corresponding lexical
map. Given a word, its spelling is first normalized and then gets
attributed a synonym class of at most eight members (using WordNet). It
then uses Ladder context seeding starting at width $`1`$, or width $`2`$
when the last mapped token ID is below $`200`$. For the hash function,
it uses the *rolling polynomial
hash* ([App. G](#A7 "Appendix G Hash Function and PRNG ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).

For the watermark score, it uses both Prelude with a cap of $`14`$ nats
of entropy or $`24`$ tokens and $`6`$ independent Channels. It uses the
Gumbel race as a logits transformation. For detection, the low variant
uses the Excess Gamma detection and the high variant the weighted
Position evidence.

1: Keys $`\xi_{0},\ldots,\xi_{5}`$, model distributions $`p_{t}`$,
lexical map $`\mathcal{G}`$, completion length $`T`$.

2: Sample $`J\sim\mathcal{U}\{0,\ldots,5\}`$ $`\triangleright`$ Use
channel $`J`$, keyed by $`\xi_{J}`$, throughout

3: $`\omega\leftarrow()`$; $`B\leftarrow 0`$;
$`\mathcal{U}\leftarrow\emptyset`$

4: for $`t=1,\ldots,T`$ do

5:   if $`t\leq 24`$ and $`B<14`$ then

6:    Sample $`\omega_{t}\sim p_{t}`$ using private randomness

7:    $`B\leftarrow B-\log\sum_{v}p_{t}(v)^{2}`$ $`\triangleright`$
Prelude collision entropy

8:   else

9:
   $`z_{1:t-1}\leftarrow(\mathcal{G}(\omega_{1}),\ldots,\mathcal{G}(\omega_{t-1}))`$;
$`m\leftarrow\min(4,t-1)`$

10:    $`\ell\leftarrow 1`$; if $`z_{t-1}<200`$, set
$`\ell\leftarrow\min(2,m)`$

11:    for $`w=\ell,\ldots,m`$ do

12:      $`W\leftarrow z_{t-w:t-1}`$ $`\triangleright`$ Suffix of width
$`w`$

13:
     $`n_{t}\leftarrow\left|\{i:w\leq i<t-1,\ z_{i-w+1:i}=W\}\right|`$
$`\triangleright`$ Count earlier occurrences

14:      If $`n_{t}<4`$ or $`w=m`$, set $`c_{t}\leftarrow(w,W,n_{t})`$,
$`a_{t}\leftarrow h(c_{t})`$ and break $`\triangleright`$ Context and
seed

15:    end for

16:    if $`n_{t}\geq 8192`$ or $`a_{t}\in\mathcal{U}`$ then

17:      Sample $`\omega_{t}\sim p_{t}`$ using private randomness

18:    else

19:      $`\mathcal{U}\leftarrow\mathcal{U}\cup\{a_{t}\}`$

20:      $`\tilde{U}_{t,v}\leftarrow U_{J,a_{t},v}`$ for each $`v`$ with
$`p_{t}(v)>0`$

21:
     $`\omega_{t}\leftarrow\arg\min_{v:p_{t}(v)>0}\{-\log\tilde{U}_{t,v}/p_{t}(v)\}`$
$`\triangleright`$ Token-level exponential race

22:    end if

23:   end if

24:   Append $`\omega_{t}`$ to $`\omega`$

25: end for

26: return $`\omega`$

Algorithm 4 ConcordMark generation

1: Keys $`\xi_{0},\ldots,\xi_{5}`$, completion $`\omega`$, lexical map
$`\mathcal{G}`$.

2: $`D\leftarrow\emptyset`$; $`\mathcal{U}\leftarrow\emptyset`$

3: for $`t=2,\ldots,|\omega|`$ do

4:   Reconstruct the ladder seed $`a_{t}`$ and count $`n_{t}`$ from
$`\mathcal{G}(\omega_{<t})`$ as
in [Algorithm 4](#alg4 "In Key components ‣ H.1 ConcordMark ‣ Appendix H ConcordMark and RotationFirst ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")

5:   If $`n_{t}<8192`$ and $`(a_{t},\omega_{t})\notin\mathcal{U}`$, set
$`D\leftarrow D\cup\{t\}`$ and
$`\mathcal{U}\leftarrow\mathcal{U}\cup\{(a_{t},\omega_{t})\}`$

6: end for

7: If $`D=\emptyset`$, return $`1`$

8: $`\mathcal{H}(\omega)\leftarrow\{a_{t}:t\in D\}`$;
$`H\leftarrow|\mathcal{H}(\omega)|`$

9: $`D_{a}(\omega)\leftarrow\{\omega_{t}:t\in D,\ a_{t}=a\}`$;
$`m_{a}\leftarrow|D_{a}(\omega)|`$ for each $`a\in\mathcal{H}(\omega)`$

10: for $`j=0,\ldots,5`$ do

11:   for $`a\in\mathcal{H}(\omega)`$ do

12:
   $`S_{j,a}(\omega)\leftarrow\sum_{v\in D_{a}(\omega)}-\log(1-U_{j,a,v})`$

13:    $`Z_{j,a}\leftarrow-\log Q(m_{a},S_{j,a}(\omega))`$
$`\triangleright`$ Calibrate each context with its Gamma tail

14:   end for

15:
  $`S_{j}(\omega)\leftarrow\sum_{a\in\mathcal{H}(\omega)}\max\{Z_{j,a}-\log 2,0\}`$
$`\triangleright`$ Keep evidence above the median

16:   $`P_{j}\leftarrow 1`$

17:   if $`S_{j}(\omega)>H/2`$ then

18:    $`\theta\leftarrow(3-\sqrt{1+4H/S_{j}(\omega)})/2`$

19:
   $`P_{j}\leftarrow\exp\{H\log[(1-\theta/2)/(1-\theta)]-\theta S_{j}(\omega)\}`$
$`\triangleright`$ Chernoff bound

20:    If $`P_{j}<0.1`$, set
$`P_{j}\leftarrow\sum_{b=1}^{H}\binom{H}{b}2^{-H}Q(b,S_{j}(\omega))`$
$`\triangleright`$ Exact excess tail $`R_{H}`$

21:   end if

22: end for

23: return $`P(\omega)=1-(1-\min_{j}P_{j})^{6}`$ $`\triangleright`$
Šidák correction over channels

Algorithm 5 ConcordMark (low) detection

1: Keys $`\xi_{0},\ldots,\xi_{5}`$, completion $`\omega`$, lexical map
$`\mathcal{G}`$, auxiliary model distributions $`\hat{p}_{t}`$.

2: Reconstruct $`a_{t}`$ and the retained positions $`D`$ as
in [Algorithm 5](#alg5 "In Key components ‣ H.1 ConcordMark ‣ Appendix H ConcordMark and RotationFirst ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")

3: If $`D=\emptyset`$, return $`1`$

4: for $`t\in D`$ do

5:
  $`\eta_{t}\leftarrow 1+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{round}\!\left(4\min\{\max\{-\log\hat{p}_{t}(\omega_{t}),0\},2.5\}\right)`$

6:
  $`C_{t}\leftarrow\{\text{eight most probable tokens under }\hat{p}_{t}\}\setminus\{\omega_{t}\}`$

7:
  $`\alpha_{t,v}\leftarrow\min\{10^{4},\hat{p}_{t}(v)/\hat{p}_{t}(\omega_{t})\}`$
for each $`v\in C_{t}`$

8:   $`C_{t}\leftarrow\{v\in C_{t}:\alpha_{t,v}\geq 10^{-3}\}`$;
$`\lambda_{t}\leftarrow\sum_{v\in C_{t}}\alpha_{t,v}`$

9:   If $`\lambda_{t}>8`$, set $`C_{t}\leftarrow\emptyset`$ and
$`\lambda_{t}\leftarrow 0`$ $`\triangleright`$ Discard an unreliable
reconstructed race

10: end for

11: for $`j=0,\ldots,5`$ do

12:   for $`t\in D`$ do

13:
   $`W_{j,t}\leftarrow\mathbf{1}\{U_{j,a_{t},v}<U_{j,a_{t},\omega_{t}}^{\alpha_{t,v}}\text{ for all }v\in C_{t}\}`$

14:    if $`W_{j,t}=1`$ then $`\triangleright`$ The observed token wins
the reconstructed race

15:
     $`R_{j,t}\leftarrow(1-U_{j,a_{t},\omega_{t}}^{1+\lambda_{t}})/(1+\lambda_{t})`$

16:    else

17:
     $`R_{j,t}\leftarrow 1-U_{j,a_{t},\omega_{t}}+U_{j,a_{t},\omega_{t}}^{1+\lambda_{t}}/(1+\lambda_{t})`$

18:    end if

19:   end for

20:   $`S_{j}(\omega)\leftarrow\sum_{t\in D}-\eta_{t}\log R_{j,t}`$
$`\triangleright`$ Weighted position evidence

21: end for

22: $`s\leftarrow\max_{j}S_{j}(\omega)`$

23: if all weights equal some $`\eta`$ then

24:   $`q\leftarrow Q(|D|,s/\eta)`$ $`\triangleright`$ Exact Gamma upper
tail

25: else

26:   $`q\leftarrow`$ Lugannani–Rice approximation to
$`\Pr[\sum_{t\in D}\eta_{t}E_{t}\geq s]`$, for independent
$`E_{t}\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$

27: end if

28: return $`P(\omega)=\min\{1,1.02[1-(1-q)^{6}]\}`$ $`\triangleright`$
Channel correction and tail safety factor

Algorithm 6 ConcordMark (high) detection

### H.2 RotationFirst

#### Key components

We describe precisely the RotationFirst generation algorithm and its
detector
in [Algorithms 7](#alg7 "In Key components ‣ H.2 RotationFirst ‣ Appendix H ConcordMark and RotationFirst ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
and [8](#alg8 "Algorithm 8 ‣ Key components ‣ H.2 RotationFirst ‣ Appendix H ConcordMark and RotationFirst ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").
RotationFirst uses Lexical group throughout the scheme. Let
$`\mathcal{G}:\Sigma\rightarrow\mathbb{N}`$ be the corresponding lexical
map. Each token is decoded, stripped of surrounding whitespace, and
lowercased. If the resulting word appears in WordNet, it is assigned to
the synonym class given by its first WordNet synset. Let $`\mathcal{E}`$
be the set of the resulting synonym classes. Tokens sharing this synset
are grouped together, whereas all other tokens remain in singleton
classes. It then uses Global first use context seeding with the
*rotation first
hash* ([App. G](#A7 "Appendix G Hash Function and PRNG ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
For a class $`c`$, it uses address $`(0,c)`$ if it has not been used
before and $`c\in\mathcal{E}`$, and otherwise uses
$`(\mathcal{G}(\omega_{t-1})+1,c)`$.

For the watermark score, it uses a *private geometry* approach, namely
the Rotation spherical geometry (Spherical). For each request, sample
randomly a uniform quaternion $`A`$. Then, at each step draw a uniform
keyed $`Z_{a_{t},u}\in S^{3}`$ and derive the score:

|     |                                                         |     |
|-----|---------------------------------------------------------|-----|
|     |
       ``` math
       \tilde{U}_{a_{t},u}=F(\lvert A\cdot Z_{a_{t},u}\rvert),
       ```                                                      |     |

where $`F(r)=\frac{2}{\pi}\bigl(\arcsin r+r\sqrt{1-r^{2}}\bigr)`$. Then
for detection, it uses the corresponding Predictive Gamma detector.

1: Key $`\xi`$, model distributions $`p_{t}`$, grouping $`\mathcal{G}`$,
eligible classes $`\mathcal{E}`$, completion length $`T`$.

2: Sample $`A\sim\mathcal{U}(\mathbb{S}^{3})`$ $`\triangleright`$
Private rotation shared throughout the completion

3: $`F(r)\leftarrow\frac{2}{\pi}(\arcsin r+r\sqrt{1-r^{2}})`$

4: $`\omega\leftarrow()`$; $`\mathcal{A}\leftarrow\emptyset`$;
$`\mathcal{U}\leftarrow\emptyset`$ $`\triangleright`$ Emitted classes
and initialized clocks

5: for $`t=1,\ldots,T`$ do

6:   $`M_{t}(u)\leftarrow\sum_{v:\mathcal{G}(v)=u}p_{t}(v)`$ for each
class $`u`$

7:   $`b_{t}\leftarrow\mathcal{G}(\omega_{t-1})+1`$ if $`t>1`$,
otherwise $`b_{t}\leftarrow 0`$

8:   for each class $`u`$ with $`M_{t}(u)>0`$ do

9:    $`c_{t}(u)\leftarrow 0`$ if
$`u\in\mathcal{E}\setminus\mathcal{A}`$, otherwise
$`c_{t}(u)\leftarrow b_{t}`$; $`a_{t}(u)\leftarrow h(c_{t}(u))`$

10:    if $`(a_{t}(u),u)\notin\mathcal{U}`$ then

11:      if $`b_{t}\neq 0`$ or $`u\in\mathcal{E}`$ then

12:       Recover $`Z_{a_{t}(u),u}\in\mathbb{S}^{3}`$ using key $`\xi`$

13:
      $`\tilde{U}_{a_{t}(u),u}\leftarrow F(|A\cdot Z_{a_{t}(u),u}|)`$

14:       $`R_{a_{t}(u),u}\leftarrow-\log\tilde{U}_{a_{t}(u),u}`$

15:      else

16:       Sample $`R_{a_{t}(u),u}\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$ privately

17:      end if

18:      $`\mathcal{U}\leftarrow\mathcal{U}\cup\{(a_{t}(u),u)\}`$

19:    end if

20:   end for

21:   $`u_{*}\leftarrow\arg\min_{u:M_{t}(u)>0}R_{a_{t}(u),u}/M_{t}(u)`$;
$`\tau_{t}\leftarrow R_{a_{t}(u_{*}),u_{*}}/M_{t}(u_{*})`$

22:
  $`R_{a_{t}(u),u}\leftarrow\max\{0,R_{a_{t}(u),u}-\tau_{t}M_{t}(u)\}`$
for each $`u`$ with $`M_{t}(u)>0`$

23:   Sample $`R_{a_{t}(u_{*}),u_{*}}\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$
privately $`\triangleright`$ Refresh the winning clock

24:   Sample $`\omega_{t}`$ from $`\{v:\mathcal{G}(v)=u_{*}\}`$ with
probabilities $`p_{t}(v)/M_{t}(u_{*})`$

25:   $`\mathcal{A}\leftarrow\mathcal{A}\cup\{u_{*}\}`$; append
$`\omega_{t}`$ to $`\omega`$

26: end for

27: return $`\omega`$

Algorithm 7 RotationFirst generation

1: Key $`\xi`$, completion $`\omega`$, grouping $`\mathcal{G}`$,
eligible classes $`\mathcal{E}`$, public unit quaternions
$`A_{0},\ldots,A_{511}`$.

2: $`D\leftarrow()`$; $`\mathcal{A}\leftarrow\emptyset`$;
$`\mathcal{U}\leftarrow\emptyset`$

3: for $`t=1,\ldots,|\omega|`$ do

4:   $`u_{t}\leftarrow\mathcal{G}(\omega_{t})`$

5:   $`b_{t}\leftarrow\mathcal{G}(\omega_{t-1})+1`$ if $`t>1`$,
otherwise $`b_{t}\leftarrow 0`$

6:   $`c_{t}\leftarrow 0`$ if
$`u_{t}\in\mathcal{E}\setminus\mathcal{A}`$, otherwise
$`c_{t}\leftarrow b_{t}`$; $`a_{t}\leftarrow h(c_{t})`$

7:   If $`(t>1\text{ or }u_{t}\in\mathcal{E})`$ and
$`(a_{t},u_{t})\notin\mathcal{U}`$, append $`(a_{t},u_{t})`$ to $`D`$
and set $`\mathcal{U}\leftarrow\mathcal{U}\cup\{(a_{t},u_{t})\}`$

8:   $`\mathcal{A}\leftarrow\mathcal{A}\cup\{u_{t}\}`$

9: end for

10: $`N\leftarrow|D|`$; if $`N\leq 1`$, return $`1`$

11: Enumerate $`D`$ as $`(a_{i},u_{i})_{i=1}^{N}`$ in text order

12: $`F(r)\leftarrow\frac{2}{\pi}(\arcsin r+r\sqrt{1-r^{2}})`$;
$`d(B,Z)\leftarrow 1-F(|B\cdot Z|)`$

13: $`B_{1}\leftarrow A_{0}`$; $`w_{1,j}\leftarrow 1/512`$ for
$`j=0,\ldots,511`$; $`S(\omega)\leftarrow 0`$

14: for $`i=1,\ldots,N`$ do

15:   Recover $`Z_{i}=Z_{a_{i},u_{i}}\in\mathbb{S}^{3}`$ using key
$`\xi`$

16:   $`S(\omega)\leftarrow S(\omega)-\log d(B_{i},Z_{i})`$
$`\triangleright`$ Score before updating the predicted rotation

17:   $`w_{i+1,j}\leftarrow w_{i,j}\,d(A_{j},Z_{i})^{-1/2}`$ for
$`j=0,\ldots,511`$

18:   Normalize
$`w_{i+1,j}\leftarrow w_{i+1,j}/\sum_{k=0}^{511}w_{i+1,k}`$

19:
  $`B_{i+1}\leftarrow\operatorname{eig}_{\max}(\sum_{j=0}^{511}w_{i+1,j}A_{j}A_{j}^{\top})`$
$`\triangleright`$ Unit eigenvector for the largest eigenvalue

20: end for

21: return $`P(\omega)=Q(N,S(\omega))`$ $`\triangleright`$ Predictive
Gamma upper tail

Algorithm 8 RotationFirst detection

### H.3 Additional Evaluation

Here, we complete the evaluation
from [Section 4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Independent Evaluation of the Best Directions ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
with additional
plots ([Figure 26](#A8.F26 "In H.3 Additional Evaluation ‣ Appendix H ConcordMark and RotationFirst ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
Namely, we plot the TPR as a function of the significance level
$`\alpha`$, from $`10^{-6}`$ to $`10^{-1}`$, for clean detection and
paraphrasing. At each $`\alpha`$, the TPR is the fraction of samples
with p-value below $`\alpha`$. As in the main evaluation, we report the
minimum TPR across the five watermarking seeds.

Figure 26: TPR as a function of the significance level $`\alpha`$, with
1k samples per model and language generated from WildChat prompts. Left
is clean detection and right after paraphrasing.

#### Results

Across models, languages, and significance levels, these curves confirm
the conclusions
of [Section 4.3](#S4.SS3 "4.3 Independent Evaluation of the Best Directions ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").
ConcordMark (high) provides the strongest detection, and especially
after paraphrasing. ConcordMark (low) also retains a strong paraphrasing
robustness while being more efficient at detection, as it does not
require a forward pass. RotationFirst is less robust than ConcordMark,
as expected as it focuses mainly on quality, yet remains comparable to
the baselines.

## Appendix I Proofs

In this section, we prove the theoretical claims made throughout the
paper.
In [Section I.1](#A9.SS1 "I.1 Preliminaries ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
we state our assumptions and two lemmas used in the rest of the section.
In [Section I.2](#A9.SS2 "I.2 Soundness Given a Key ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
we prove that a detector that is sound over the key can be turned into a
detector that is sound given a
key ([Section 3.2](#S3.SS2 "3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
In [Section I.3](#A9.SS3 "I.3 Validity of the Verification Tests ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
we prove that the three statistical tests
of [Section 3.3](#S3.SS3 "3.3 Automatic Verification ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
are valid.
In [Section I.4](#A9.SS4 "I.4 Distortion-Freeness of Residual Clocks ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
we prove that ResidualRace is
distortion-free ([Section A.5](#A1.SS5 "A.5 Logits Transformation ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
Lastly,
in [Section I.5](#A9.SS5 "I.5 Validity of the Detectors ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
we derive the null distribution of the Predictive Gamma and Position
evidence
detectors ([Section A.6](#A1.SS6 "A.6 Detection ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
For all other mathematical results, we consider the proof sufficiently
trivial and do not derive them here.

### I.1 Preliminaries

#### Setup

Let $`\Xi`$ be the key space, and let $`\xi`$ be drawn from $`\Xi`$ as
in [Equation 2](#S3.E2 "In Soundness over the key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").
For every text $`\omega\in\Sigma^{*}`$, the detector returns a p-value
$`P_{\xi}(\omega)\in[0,1]`$, and we assume that
$`(\xi,\omega)\mapsto P_{\xi}(\omega)`$ is measurable (which holds
trivially for a finite key space). Human texts are written without
knowledge of the private key: for any human text distribution
$`\mathcal{H}_{0}`$, the text $`\Omega\sim\mathcal{H}_{0}`$ is
independent of $`\xi`$. As
in [Section 3.1](#S3.SS1 "3.1 Preliminaries on LLM Watermarks ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
we model the PRNG as ideal: the seed $`a_{t}`$ is a function of the
context only, and, over a uniformly drawn key, the scores of distinct
(seed, unit) pairs are independent, with
$`U_{a,u}\sim\mathcal{U}([0,1])`$ (and $`Z_{a,u}`$ distributed according
to its geometry for private-geometry scores). We also assume that the
hash function has no
collision ([App. G](#A7 "Appendix G Hash Function and PRNG ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
Finally, we write
$`T(s,p,c)\mathrel{:=}\Pr_{Z\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(s,p)}[Z\geq c]`$ for
the binomial upper tail, as
in [Algorithm 3](#alg3 "In Appendix F Statistical Tests ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").

###### Lemma 1.

Let $`X`$ be a real random variable and
$`\varphi:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow[0,\infty)`$ a continuous nonincreasing
function such that $`\Pr[X\geq s]\leq\varphi(s)`$ for all
$`s\in\mathbb{R}`$. Then $`\min\{1,\varphi(X)\}`$ is a valid p-value,
i.e., $`\Pr[\min\{1,\varphi(X)\}\leq x]\leq x`$ for all $`x\in[0,1]`$.

###### Proof.

The case $`x=1`$ is trivial, and the case $`x=0`$ follows from the case
$`x>0`$, since
$`\Pr[\min\{1,\varphi(X)\}\leq 0]\leq\Pr[\min\{1,\varphi(X)\}\leq x]`$
for every $`x>0`$. Let $`x\in(0,1)`$ and
$`I\mathrel{:=}\{s\in\mathbb{R}:\varphi(s)\leq x\}`$. If
$`I=\emptyset`$, the event is empty. Otherwise, $`I`$ is an interval
unbounded above, and it is bounded below, since otherwise
$`\Pr[X\geq s]\leq x<1`$ for all $`s`$, which contradicts
$`\Pr[X\geq s]\rightarrow 1`$ as $`s\rightarrow-\infty`$. Let
$`s^{*}\mathrel{:=}\inf I`$. By continuity, $`\varphi(s^{*})\leq x`$,
and since $`\{\varphi(X)\leq x\}\subseteq\{X\geq s^{*}\}`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Pr[\min\{1,\varphi(X)\}\leq x]\leq\Pr[X\geq s^{*}]\leq\varphi(s^{*})\leq x.\qed
``` |  |

###### Lemma 2.

Let $`X`$ be a sum of $`s`$ independent Bernoulli random variables with
parameters at most $`p\in[0,1]`$. Then $`\Pr[X\geq c]\leq T(s,p,c)`$ for
all $`c\in\mathbb{N}`$, and $`\Pr[T(s,p,X)\leq\eta]\leq\eta`$ for all
$`\eta\in[0,1]`$.

###### Proof.

Let $`p_{1},\dots,p_{s}\leq p`$ be the Bernoulli parameters and
$`V_{1},\dots,V_{s}`$ i.i.d. uniform random variables on $`[0,1]`$. Then
$`X`$ has the same distribution as
$`\sum_{i}\mathds{1}\{V_{i}\leq p_{i}\}\leq\sum_{i}\mathds{1}\{V_{i}\leq p\}\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(s,p)`$,
which gives the first claim. For the second claim, since
$`c\mapsto T(s,p,c)`$ is nonincreasing and $`T(s,p,s+1)=0`$, let
$`c^{*}\mathrel{:=}\min\{c\in\{0,\dots,s+1\}:T(s,p,c)\leq\eta\}`$. Then
$`\{T(s,p,X)\leq\eta\}=\{X\geq c^{*}\}`$, and by the first claim,
$`\Pr[X\geq c^{*}]\leq T(s,p,c^{*})\leq\eta`$. ∎

### I.2 Soundness Given a Key

We prove the claim
of [Section 3.2](#S3.SS2 "3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"):
multiplying by $`1/\beta`$ the p-value of a detector that is sound over
the
key ([Equation 2](#S3.E2 "In Soundness over the key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"))
gives a detector that is sound given a
key ([Equation 3](#S3.E3 "In Soundness given a key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).

###### Proposition 1.

Let $`\beta\in(0,1]`$ and let $`P_{\xi}`$ be a detector that
satisfies [Equation 2](#S3.E2 "In Soundness over the key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").
Define the calibrated detector

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
P^{\beta}_{\xi}(\omega)\mathrel{:=}\min\left\{1,\frac{P_{\xi}(\omega)}{\beta}\right\}.
``` |  | (14) |

Then $`P^{\beta}_{\xi}`$
satisfies [Equation 2](#S3.E2 "In Soundness over the key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
and for every human text distribution $`\mathcal{H}_{0}`$ and every
$`\alpha\in[0,1]`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Pr_{\xi}\left[\Pr_{\Omega\sim\mathcal{H}_{0}}[P^{\beta}_{\xi}(\Omega)\leq\alpha]>\alpha\right]\leq\beta,
``` |  |

i.e., $`P^{\beta}_{\xi}`$ also
satisfies [Equation 3](#S3.E3 "In Soundness given a key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").

###### Proof.

We first relate the rejection regions of both detectors. For
$`\alpha\in[0,1)`$, since $`\min\{1,x\}\leq\alpha<1`$ holds if and only
if $`x\leq\alpha`$, we have for every key $`\xi`$ and text $`\omega`$

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
P^{\beta}_{\xi}(\omega)\leq\alpha\iff P_{\xi}(\omega)\leq\alpha\beta.
``` |  | (15) |

For $`\alpha=1`$, both properties hold trivially, as all probabilities
are bounded by $`1`$. We therefore assume $`\alpha\in[0,1)`$ in the rest
of the proof.

*Soundness over the key.* Let $`\omega\in\Sigma^{*}`$.
By [Equation 15](#A9.E15 "In Proof. ‣ I.2 Soundness Given a Key ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
and [Equation 2](#S3.E2 "In Soundness over the key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
applied at the threshold $`\alpha\beta\in[0,1]`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Pr_{\xi}[P^{\beta}_{\xi}(\omega)\leq\alpha]=\Pr_{\xi}[P_{\xi}(\omega)\leq\alpha\beta]\leq\alpha\beta\leq\alpha.
``` |  |

*Soundness given a key.* Let $`\mathcal{H}_{0}`$ be a human text
distribution, and define for each key the false positive rate

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
g(\xi)\mathrel{:=}\Pr_{\Omega\sim\mathcal{H}_{0}}[P^{\beta}_{\xi}(\Omega)\leq\alpha]=\Pr_{\Omega\sim\mathcal{H}_{0}}[P_{\xi}(\Omega)\leq\alpha\beta],
``` |  |

where the equality follows
from [Equation 15](#A9.E15 "In Proof. ‣ I.2 Soundness Given a Key ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").
Because $`\Omega`$ is independent of $`\xi`$, Fubini’s theorem allows us
to swap the two expectations, and
applying [Equation 2](#S3.E2 "In Soundness over the key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
to each fixed text gives

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbb{E}_{\xi}[g(\xi)]=\Pr_{\xi,\Omega}[P_{\xi}(\Omega)\leq\alpha\beta]=\mathbb{E}_{\Omega\sim\mathcal{H}_{0}}\left[\Pr_{\xi}[P_{\xi}(\Omega)\leq\alpha\beta]\right]\leq\alpha\beta.
``` |  |

If $`\alpha=0`$, then $`g\geq 0`$ and
$`\mathbb{E}_{\xi}[g(\xi)]\leq 0`$, so $`g(\xi)=0`$ almost surely and
$`\Pr_{\xi}[g(\xi)>0]=0\leq\beta`$. Otherwise, $`\alpha>0`$ and Markov’s
inequality gives

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Pr_{\xi}[g(\xi)>\alpha]\leq\frac{\mathbb{E}_{\xi}[g(\xi)]}{\alpha}\leq\frac{\alpha\beta}{\alpha}=\beta,
``` |  |

which concludes the proof. ∎

### I.3 Validity of the Verification Tests

We prove that each of the three tests
of [Section 3.3](#S3.SS3 "3.3 Automatic Verification ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
wrongly rejects a valid scheme with probability at most its significance
level $`\delta`$.

###### Proposition 2.

Let $`f`$ be a distortion-free logits
transformation ([Equation 1](#S3.E1 "In Additional requirements ‣ 3.1 Preliminaries on LLM Watermarks ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
For each context $`t`$, let $`v_{1},\dots,v_{k}`$ be the $`k`$ most
likely tokens under $`p_{t}`$ and let

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
G_{t}(q)\mathrel{:=}\Bigl(q(v_{1}),\dots,q(v_{k}),1-\sum_{r=1}^{k}q(v_{r})\Bigr)
``` |  |

map a distribution $`q\in\Delta(\Sigma)`$ to a probability vector over
the head tokens and the pooled remaining tokens. For $`m`$ independent
keys, let
$`d_{j}\mathrel{:=}G_{t}(f(\zeta_{t}^{(j)},p_{t}))-G_{t}(p_{t})`$,
$`\bar{d}`$ their mean, $`h\mathrel{:=}\lfloor m/2\rfloor`$,
$`u\mathrel{:=}\mathrm{sign}(h^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{h}d_{j})`$ and
$`b\mathrel{:=}\max\{0,(m-h)^{-1}\sum_{j=h+1}^{m}u^{\top}d_{j}\}`$.
[Algorithm 1](#alg1 "In Appendix F Statistical Tests ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
combines the p-values

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
p_{\mathrm{coord}}\mathrel{:=}\min\{1,2(k+1)\exp(-2m\lVert\bar{d}\rVert_{\infty}^{2})\}\quad\text{and}\quad p_{\mathrm{split}}\mathrel{:=}\exp(-(m-h)b^{2}/2)
``` |  |

into
$`q_{t}\mathrel{:=}\min\{1,2\min(p_{\mathrm{coord}},p_{\mathrm{split}})\}`$,
and rejects $`f`$ if
$`Q\mathrel{:=}\min\{1,N\min_{t}q_{t}\}\leq\delta`$.
Then [Algorithm 1](#alg1 "In Appendix F Statistical Tests ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
rejects $`f`$ with probability at most $`\delta`$.

###### Proof.

Fix a context $`t`$. Because the $`m`$ keys are drawn independently, the
scores $`\zeta_{t}^{(1)},\dots,\zeta_{t}^{(m)}`$ are i.i.d., and
by [Equation 1](#S3.E1 "In Additional requirements ‣ 3.1 Preliminaries on LLM Watermarks ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
the differences $`d_{1},\dots,d_{m}`$ are i.i.d. with
$`\mathbb{E}[d_{j}]=G_{t}(\mathbb{E}[f(\zeta_{t}^{(j)},p_{t})])-G_{t}(p_{t})=0`$,
as $`G_{t}`$ is affine.

*Coordinate test.* Each coordinate of $`G_{t}(q)`$ lies in $`[0,1]`$ for
every $`q\in\Delta(\Sigma)`$, so each coordinate of $`d_{j}`$ lies in an
interval of length $`1`$. By Hoeffding’s inequality and a union bound
over the $`k+1`$ coordinates,
$`\Pr[\lVert\bar{d}\rVert_{\infty}\geq s]\leq 2(k+1)\exp(-2ms^{2})`$ for
all $`s\geq 0`$. Hence,
by [Lemma 1](#Thmlemma1 "Lemma 1. ‣ Setup ‣ I.1 Preliminaries ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
with $`\varphi(s)=2(k+1)\exp(-2ms^{2})`$, $`p_{\mathrm{coord}}`$ is a
valid p-value.

*Split test.* The direction $`u`$ only depends on $`d_{1},\dots,d_{h}`$,
so conditional on $`u`$, the variables
$`Y_{j}\mathrel{:=}u^{\top}d_{j}`$ for $`j>h`$ are i.i.d. with mean
zero. Since $`G_{t}(q)`$ and $`G_{t}(p_{t})`$ are probability vectors
and $`u\in[-1,1]^{k+1}`$, $`u^{\top}G_{t}(q)\in[-1,1]`$ and hence
$`Y_{j}`$ lies in an interval of length $`2`$. By Hoeffding’s
inequality, $`\Pr[b\geq s\mid u]\leq\exp(-(m-h)s^{2}/2)`$ for all
$`s>0`$, where $`m-h\geq 1`$ as $`m\geq 2`$. Hence,
by [Lemma 1](#Thmlemma1 "Lemma 1. ‣ Setup ‣ I.1 Preliminaries ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
with $`\varphi(s)=\exp(-(m-h)s^{2}/2)`$, $`p_{\mathrm{split}}`$ is a
valid p-value conditional on $`u`$, and thus unconditionally.

*Combination.* By a union bound over both tests,
$`\Pr[q_{t}\leq x]\leq\Pr[p_{\mathrm{coord}}\leq x/2]+\Pr[p_{\mathrm{split}}\leq x/2]\leq x`$.
By a union bound over the $`N`$ contexts,
$`\Pr[Q\leq\delta]\leq\sum_{t=1}^{N}\Pr[q_{t}\leq\delta/N]\leq\delta`$.
∎

###### Proposition 3.

Let $`P_{\xi}`$ be a detector that is sound over the
key ([Equation 2](#S3.E2 "In Soundness over the key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")),
i.e.,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\forall\omega\in\Sigma^{*},\forall\alpha\in[0,1],\quad\Pr_{\xi}[P_{\xi}(\omega)\leq\alpha]\leq\alpha.
``` |  |

Given a corpus $`C=(\omega_{1},\dots,\omega_{n})`$, thresholds
$`\mathcal{A}`$ and $`m`$ independent keys
$`\xi_{1}^{i},\dots,\xi_{m}^{i}`$ per text,
[Algorithm 2](#alg2 "In Appendix F Statistical Tests ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
counts the false positives
$`X_{i}(\alpha)\mathrel{:=}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\mathds{1}\{P_{\xi_{j}^{i}}(\omega_{i})\leq\alpha\}`$,
and rejects $`P_{\xi}`$ if
$`q_{i}(\alpha)\mathrel{:=}T(m,\alpha,X_{i}(\alpha))\leq\eta\mathrel{:=}(1-(1-\delta)^{1/n})/|\mathcal{A}|`$
for some text $`\omega_{i}`$ and threshold $`\alpha\in\mathcal{A}`$.
Then, for every corpus
$`C`$, [Algorithm 2](#alg2 "In Appendix F Statistical Tests ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
rejects $`P_{\xi}`$ with probability at most $`\delta`$.

###### Proof.

Fix a text $`\omega_{i}`$ and a threshold $`\alpha\in\mathcal{A}`$.
Because the keys $`\xi_{1}^{i},\dots,\xi_{m}^{i}`$ are i.i.d.,
$`X_{i}(\alpha)`$ is a sum of $`m`$ i.i.d. Bernoulli random variables
with parameter $`\Pr_{\xi}[P_{\xi}(\omega_{i})\leq\alpha]\leq\alpha`$ by
soundness over the key. Hence,
by [Lemma 2](#Thmlemma2 "Lemma 2. ‣ Setup ‣ I.1 Preliminaries ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
$`\Pr[q_{i}(\alpha)\leq\eta]\leq\eta`$, and by a union bound over the
thresholds, the event
$`E_{i}\mathrel{:=}\{\exists\alpha\in\mathcal{A}:q_{i}(\alpha)\leq\eta\}`$
has probability at most $`|\mathcal{A}|\eta=1-(1-\delta)^{1/n}`$. The
events $`E_{1},\dots,E_{n}`$ depend on disjoint sets of independent
keys, so they are independent, and

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Pr[\mathcal{R}\neq\emptyset]=1-\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1-\Pr[E_{i}])\leq 1-(1-\delta)=\delta.\qed
``` |  |

###### Proposition 4.

Let $`P_{\xi}`$ be a detector that is sound given a
key ([Equation 3](#S3.E3 "In Soundness given a key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"))
for the human text distribution $`\mathcal{H}_{0}`$, the fraction
$`\beta`$, and the thresholds $`\mathcal{A}`$, i.e.,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\forall\alpha\in\mathcal{A},\quad\Pr_{\xi}[\Pr_{\Omega\sim\mathcal{H}_{0}}[P_{\xi}(\Omega)\leq\alpha]>\alpha]\leq\beta.
``` |  |

[Algorithm 3](#alg3 "In Appendix F Statistical Tests ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
draws $`d`$ independent keys $`\xi_{j}`$ and, for each key, $`n`$
independent texts
$`\omega_{1}^{j},\dots,\omega_{n}^{j}\sim\mathcal{H}_{0}`$, and counts
the false positives
$`X_{j}(\alpha)\mathrel{:=}\sum_{t=1}^{n}\mathds{1}\{P_{\xi_{j}}(\omega_{t}^{j})\leq\alpha\}`$.
For each threshold $`\alpha\in\mathcal{A}`$ and screening level
$`\gamma`$ in a predeclared finite set $`\mathcal{S}\subset(0,1)`$, a
key screens positive if $`X_{j}(\alpha)\geq c`$, where
$`c\mathrel{:=}\min\{k\in\{1,\dots,n+1\}:T(n,\alpha,k)\leq\gamma\}`$ is
the smallest count that is significant at level $`\gamma`$ for a key
with false positive rate $`\alpha`$. Let $`r\mathrel{:=}T(n,\alpha,c)`$,
$`b\mathrel{:=}\beta+(1-\beta)r`$, and $`B`$ the number of keys that
screen positive.
[Algorithm 3](#alg3 "In Appendix F Statistical Tests ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
rejects $`P_{\xi}`$ if
$`q\mathrel{:=}T(d,b,B)\leq\eta\mathrel{:=}\delta/(|\mathcal{A}||\mathcal{S}|)`$
for some $`(\alpha,\gamma)\in\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{S}`$.
Then [Algorithm 3](#alg3 "In Appendix F Statistical Tests ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
rejects $`P_{\xi}`$ with probability at most $`\delta`$.

###### Proof.

Fix $`(\alpha,\gamma)\in\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{S}`$, and note that
$`c`$, $`r`$ and $`b`$ are deterministic. For a key $`\xi`$, let
$`g(\xi)\mathrel{:=}\Pr_{\Omega\sim\mathcal{H}_{0}}[P_{\xi}(\Omega)\leq\alpha]`$
be its false positive rate, and say that $`\xi`$ is bad if
$`g(\xi)>\alpha`$. Given $`\xi_{j}`$, the texts
$`\omega_{1}^{j},\dots,\omega_{n}^{j}`$ are i.i.d., so
$`X_{j}(\alpha)\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(n,g(\xi_{j}))`$. If $`\xi_{j}`$ is
not bad, $`g(\xi_{j})\leq\alpha`$,
and [Lemma 2](#Thmlemma2 "Lemma 2. ‣ Setup ‣ I.1 Preliminaries ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
gives $`\Pr[X_{j}(\alpha)\geq c\mid\xi_{j}]\leq T(n,\alpha,c)=r`$. As a
key is bad with probability $`\pi\leq\beta`$ by soundness given a key,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Pr[X_{j}(\alpha)\geq c]\leq\pi+(1-\pi)r=r+\pi(1-r)\leq\beta+(1-\beta)r=b.
``` |  |

Since all draws are independent across keys, $`B`$ is a sum of $`d`$
independent Bernoulli random variables with parameters at most $`b`$,
and
by [Lemma 2](#Thmlemma2 "Lemma 2. ‣ Setup ‣ I.1 Preliminaries ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
$`\Pr[q\leq\eta]\leq\eta`$. By a union bound over
$`\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{S}`$,
$`\Pr[\mathcal{R}\neq\emptyset]\leq|\mathcal{A}||\mathcal{S}|\eta=\delta`$.
∎

### I.4 Distortion-Freeness of Residual Clocks

We prove that
ResidualRace ([Equation 6](#S4.E6 "In Logits transformation ‣ 4.2 Breakdown of the Agent Research Directions ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"))
is distortion-free even when a context is repeated within a request,
whereas the Gumbel race requires the per-request cache for
that ([Section A.3](#A1.SS3 "A.3 Context Seeding ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
The proof relies on the following classical property of exponential
races.

###### Lemma 3.

Let $`E_{1},\dots,E_{K}`$ be i.i.d. $`\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$ random
variables and $`m_{1},\dots,m_{K}>0`$ with $`\sum_{k}m_{k}=1`$. Let
$`\tau\mathrel{:=}\min_{k}E_{k}/m_{k}`$ and
$`\kappa\mathrel{:=}\arg\min_{k}E_{k}/m_{k}`$. Then
$`\Pr[\kappa=k]=m_{k}`$, and conditional on $`(\tau,\kappa)`$, the
residuals $`(E_{j}-\tau m_{j})_{j\neq\kappa}`$ are i.i.d.
$`\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$.

###### Proof.

Since $`E_{k}/m_{k}`$ has density $`m_{k}e^{-m_{k}s}`$, for all $`k`$,
$`s\geq 0`$ and $`x_{j}\geq 0`$,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Pr[\kappa=k,\tau\in\mathrm{d}s,E_{j}-sm_{j}>x_{j}\ \forall j\neq k]=m_{k}e^{-m_{k}s}\,\mathrm{d}s\prod_{j\neq k}e^{-(sm_{j}+x_{j})}=m_{k}\cdot e^{-s}\,\mathrm{d}s\cdot\prod_{j\neq k}e^{-x_{j}}.
``` |  |

The density factorizes, so $`\kappa`$, $`\tau`$ and the residuals are
independent with the claimed distributions. ∎

###### Proposition 5.

Assume that the initial scores $`\tilde{U}_{a,u}`$ of distinct (seed,
unit) pairs are i.i.d. uniform. Then, for ResidualRace,
$`\Pr[\omega_{t}=v\mid\omega_{<t}]=p_{t}(v)`$ for every step $`t`$ and
token $`v\in\Sigma`$, even if the seed $`a_{t}`$ has already been used
in the request.

###### Proof.

Let $`\mathcal{F}_{t}`$ be the information generated by
$`\omega_{\leq t}`$ and the race outcomes
$`(\tau_{s},u_{s})_{s\leq t}`$. We show by induction the invariant:
conditional on $`\mathcal{F}_{t}`$, the current clocks $`R_{a,u}`$ of
all (seed, unit) pairs are i.i.d. $`\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$, where we
identify a clock that is not yet initialized with its initial value
$`-\log\tilde{U}_{a,u}`$. At $`t=0`$, this holds because
$`-\log\tilde{U}_{a,u}\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$.

Assume the invariant holds at $`t-1`$. Given $`\mathcal{F}_{t-1}`$, the
distribution $`p_{t}`$, the masses $`M_{t}`$ and the seed $`a_{t}`$ are
fixed, and the race
of [Equation 6](#S4.E6 "In Logits transformation ‣ 4.2 Breakdown of the Agent Research Directions ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
is an exponential race over the i.i.d. $`\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$ clocks
$`R_{a_{t},u}`$ with weights $`M_{t}(u)`$.
By [Lemma 3](#Thmlemma3 "Lemma 3. ‣ I.4 Distortion-Freeness of Residual Clocks ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
$`\Pr[u_{t}=u\mid\mathcal{F}_{t-1}]=M_{t}(u)`$, and since the token is
then sampled inside $`u_{t}`$ with private randomness,

|  |  |  |
|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\Pr[\omega_{t}=v\mid\mathcal{F}_{t-1}]=M_{t}(\mathcal{G}(v))\cdot\frac{p_{t}(v)}{M_{t}(\mathcal{G}(v))}=p_{t}(v).
``` |  |

Because $`p_{t}`$ is a function of $`\omega_{<t}`$, taking the
expectation given $`\omega_{<t}`$ proves the claim at step $`t`$. For
the invariant,
by [Lemma 3](#Thmlemma3 "Lemma 3. ‣ I.4 Distortion-Freeness of Residual Clocks ‣ Appendix I Proofs ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
conditional on $`\mathcal{F}_{t-1}`$ and $`(\tau_{t},u_{t})`$, the
updated losing clocks $`R_{a_{t},u}-\tau_{t}M_{t}(u)`$ are i.i.d.
$`\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$. The winning clock is replaced by a fresh
$`\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$, and all other clocks (other seeds, or units
with $`M_{t}(u)=0`$) are unchanged and independent of the race. The
token $`\omega_{t}`$ only depends on independent private randomness, so
the invariant holds at $`t`$. ∎

### I.5 Validity of the Detectors

We derive the null distribution of the detectors
of [Section A.6](#A1.SS6 "A.6 Detection ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
whose validity is not immediate. Throughout, the text $`\omega`$ is
fixed and the randomness is over the key only, so that an exact null
distribution
implies [Equation 2](#S3.E2 "In Soundness over the key ‣ 3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").

###### Proposition 6.

Assume that, for every fixed geometry $`B`$ and every score $`Z`$ drawn
according to its geometry, $`d(B,Z)\sim\mathcal{U}([0,1])`$. Then, for
every text $`\omega`$, the Predictive Gamma statistic
of [Equation 12](#A1.E12 "In Predictive Gamma ‣ A.6 Detection ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
satisfies $`S(\omega)\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(N,1)`$.

###### Proof.

The retained pairs $`D`$ only depend on $`\omega`$, so $`N`$ is fixed
and, by the ideal PRNG assumption, $`Z_{1},\dots,Z_{N}`$ are i.i.d. The
estimate $`B_{i}`$ is computed from $`A_{0},\dots,A_{K-1}`$ and
$`Z_{1},\dots,Z_{i-1}`$ only, and $`Z_{i}`$ is independent of
$`(Z_{1},\dots,Z_{i-1})`$. Hence, conditional on
$`Z_{1},\dots,Z_{i-1}`$, $`B_{i}`$ is fixed and
$`d_{i}=d(B_{i},Z_{i})\sim\mathcal{U}([0,1])`$. Since
$`d_{1},\dots,d_{i-1}`$ are functions of $`Z_{1},\dots,Z_{i-1}`$,
$`d_{i}`$ is independent of $`(d_{1},\dots,d_{i-1})`$, and by induction
$`d_{1},\dots,d_{N}`$ are i.i.d. uniform. Thus, the $`-\log d_{i}`$ are
i.i.d. $`\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$ and
$`S(\omega)\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(N,1)`$. ∎

###### Proposition 7.

Assume that $`\hat{p}_{t}`$ only depends on $`\omega_{<t}`$. Then, for
every text $`\omega`$, the variables $`(R_{t})_{t\in D_{\mathrm{pos}}}`$
of the Position evidence detector are i.i.d. uniform on $`[0,1]`$. In
particular,
$`S(\omega)\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(\lvert D_{\mathrm{pos}}\rvert,1)`$,
and the weighted statistic
$`\sum_{t\in D_{\mathrm{pos}}}-\eta_{t}\log R_{t}`$ has the distribution
of $`\sum_{t\in D_{\mathrm{pos}}}\eta_{t}E_{t}`$ for i.i.d.
$`E_{t}\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)`$.

###### Proof.

Since $`\hat{p}_{t}`$ only depends on $`\omega_{<t}`$, the competitors
$`C_{t}`$, the exponents $`\alpha_{t,v}`$, $`\lambda_{t}`$ and the
weights $`\eta_{t}`$ are fixed. The seeds $`a_{t}`$ for
$`t\in D_{\mathrm{pos}}`$ are distinct and $`\omega_{t}\notin C_{t}`$,
so all scores $`U_{a_{t},\omega_{t}}`$ and $`U_{a_{t},v}`$ for
$`v\in C_{t}`$ are distinct (seed, token) pairs, and are therefore
independent and uniform. In particular, each $`R_{t}`$ is a function of
its own disjoint set of scores, so the $`R_{t}`$ are independent, and it
remains to show that each $`R_{t}`$ is uniform.

Fix $`t`$ and write $`U\mathrel{:=}U_{a_{t},\omega_{t}}`$,
$`\lambda\mathrel{:=}\lambda_{t}`$ and $`W\mathrel{:=}W_{t}`$. Given
$`U=u`$, the competitors are independent, so
$`\Pr[W=1\mid U=u]=\prod_{v\in C_{t}}\Pr[U_{a_{t},v}<u^{\alpha_{t,v}}]=u^{\lambda}`$.
Let $`Y\mathrel{:=}W+U`$, which ranks every winning outcome above every
losing one, and then by the value of $`U`$. $`Y`$ has a continuous
distribution, and its survival function is, for $`W=1`$ and for $`W=0`$
respectively,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\Pr[Y^{\prime}\geq 1+u]`$ | $`\displaystyle=\int_{u}^{1}x^{\lambda}\,\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1-u^{1+\lambda}}{1+\lambda},`$ |  |
|  | $`\displaystyle\Pr[Y^{\prime}\geq u]`$ | $`\displaystyle=\frac{1}{1+\lambda}+\int_{u}^{1}(1-x^{\lambda})\,\mathrm{d}x=1-u+\frac{u^{1+\lambda}}{1+\lambda},`$ |  |

where $`Y^{\prime}`$ is an independent copy of $`Y`$. Hence
$`R_{t}=\Pr[Y^{\prime}\geq Y\mid Y]`$, and by the probability integral
transform, $`R_{t}\sim\mathcal{U}([0,1])`$. ∎

Detection ([Section A.6](#A1.SS6 "A.6 Detection ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")),
on fixed generated texts: only the detector changes, so the quality is
that of the generation. Each cell reports identity grouping / Lexical

#### Setup

We use the private evaluation
of [Section 4](#S4 "4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"):
for each metric, we report the worst result over the $`5`$ watermark
keys, each evaluated on $`1000`$ replies. We evaluate every scheme under
the three p-value corrections
of [App. C](#A3 "Appendix C Studying the Soundness Given a Key ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"):
*guaranteed* (p-values multiplied by $`1/\beta=20`$), *empirical*
(smallest multiplier $`\kappa\geq 1`$ that passes our soundness
tests, [Figure 24](#A3.F24 "In Experimental setup ‣ Appendix C Studying the Soundness Given a Key ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")),
and *no correction* ($`\kappa=1`$). As
in [App. C](#A3 "Appendix C Studying the Soundness Given a Key ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
we first remove the outer multiplier chosen by the agent (if any) and
keep the rest of the detector unchanged. For each watermark key, all
settings share the same generated replies and the same attacked texts:
only the multiplier applied to the p-values changes. Hence, the quality
columns do not depend on the setting.

#### Reading the table

Each TPR cell reports the guaranteed / empirical / no-correction
results, and the first column gives the submission index (i.e., the
x-axis
of [Figure 2](#S4.F2 "In 4.1 Autoresearch Trajectories ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
Parentheses mark the results without correction of the schemes that then
fail our soundness given a key test (i.e., whose empirical multiplier is
above $`1`$). Note
that [Figure 2](#S4.F2 "In 4.1 Autoresearch Trajectories ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
instead uses the multiplier chosen by each agent: $`20`$ for GPT-6 Astra
(except for the first two submissions of the low variant), between $`1`$
and $`6`$ for Opus 5, and none for Gemini-3.8 Flash and the baselines.
Moreover, as we evaluate the settings on newly generated replies (with
the same watermark keys), the results can differ by a few points from
those
of [Figure 2](#S4.F2 "In 4.1 Autoresearch Trajectories ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks").

### K.2 Component Ablation

[Tables 6](#A11.T6 "In K.1 Autoresearch Trajectories ‣ Appendix K Full Experimental Results ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
[7](#A11.T7 "Table 7 ‣ K.1 Autoresearch Trajectories ‣ Appendix K Full Experimental Results ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
[8](#A11.T8 "Table 8 ‣ K.1 Autoresearch Trajectories ‣ Appendix K Full Experimental Results ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
and [9](#A11.T9 "Table 9 ‣ K.1 Autoresearch Trajectories ‣ Appendix K Full Experimental Results ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
report all the configurations of the component ablation
of [App. A](#A1 "Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
following the same structure: watermark unit and context seeding,
watermark score, logits transformation, and detection.

#### Setup

We use the experimental setup
of [Section A.1](#A1.SS1 "A.1 Preliminaries and Notation ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"):
each configuration swaps one or a few components of the simple baseline
scheme (identity grouping, Fixed-length context seeding with $`k=2`$,
$`\tilde{U}=U`$, the Gumbel race, and the Gamma detector). All
configurations are evaluated on the private evaluation
of [Section 4](#S4 "4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")
with a single watermark key, and their p-values are multiplied by
$`1/\beta=20`$ so that they are sound given a
key ([Section 3.2](#S3.SS2 "3.2 What Defines a Valid Watermarking Scheme ‣ 3 Method ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks")).
Unlike the bar plots
of [App. A](#A1 "Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
which show differences, we report absolute values with the same columns
as [Table 1](#S4.T1 "In Context seeding ‣ 4.2 Breakdown of the Agent Research Directions ‣ 4 Evaluation ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"):
the TPR@1%FPR on clean text and under each attack, and the relative
distance (in %) to the unwatermarked model in perplexity and bigram and
trigram Self-BLEU.

#### Reading the tables

Each cell reports the result with the identity grouping (left) and with
the Lexical
group ([Section A.2](#A1.SS2 "A.2 Watermark Unit ‣ Appendix A Breakdown of All Generated Components ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"))
(right), so that comparing the two sides of a cell gives the effect of
the watermark unit on that configuration. The first row of each table is
the baseline scheme, which every other configuration modifies.
In [Table 9](#A11.T9 "In K.1 Autoresearch Trajectories ‣ Appendix K Full Experimental Results ‣ AutoMark: Enabling Autoresearch toDiscover Better LLM Watermarks"),
only the detector changes: each block rescores the exact same generated
texts, so the quality columns are those of the corresponding generation.
A dash indicates a configuration that we only evaluated with the
identity grouping.
````
